newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eramet down on report chairman may quit.
newsitem.headline: Eramet down on report chairman may quit.

text.p: Shares in nickel producer Eramet closed down seven francs at 303 on Friday on a report that chairman Yves Rambaud may have to leave the company if a proposed change in the group's legal status goes through.

The newspaper Le Monde reported in its October 4 edition that the French government wanted to turn Eramet into a company with both a supervisory and management board. This change "would allow a change in the leadership," it said.
A portfolio manager said Rambaud was well regarded in the financial community for his clear strategy and diversification into rapid steel and manganese activities that raised returns.
Eramet officials said state-controlled holding company Erap had called a board meeting for October 8 to study a change in the company's legal status.

Le Monde also reported that the French government favoured a plan by local groups in New Caledonia, a French territory, and Canadian firm Falconbridge to build a nickel plant in northern New Caledonia which would compete with Eramet's mines there.
Eramet officials also said they had been assured that their mining interests were not threatened.
Cholet Dupont changed its recommendation on the stock to 'lighten' from 'buy' on Friday, saying its political risk was higher than that of other nickel producers.
